Date: 2027-03-30
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Orion Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Orion Infra), Priya Desai (Orion PM)
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on finalizing model selection and pinning strategy. Reviewed latest bench results, discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, confirmed canary and rollback approach, and agreed on next steps: share spreadsheet, run throughput test, prepare rollout playbook, and deliver security artifacts.
transcript: [00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 45 minute sync, marco and sofia from my side, aisha, tom, priya from orion? can you confirm?
[00:07] Aisha Khan: yes hi all, i'm here, thanks Lena, curious to see the latest numbers, we ran some inference last night
[00:12] Tom Reynolds: here, and i have the env ready for whatever you want us to test, reminder we're on 8xA100-ish in our dev cluster
[00:18] Priya Desai: here, just interested in how pinning affects app latency for customer facing flows
[00:25] Marco Ruiz: quick agenda - 1) bench recap 2) pin recommendation 3) canary/rollback 4) next steps, sound good?
[00:30] Aisha Khan: yep go ahead

[01:02] Marco Ruiz: ok bench recap: we ran the 3k and 4k context slices against model-redwood-13b-v2 and model-redwood-70b-q4 (note the 70b is quantized), results were - 13b avg p95 token-latency ~110ms on our infra, 70b-q4 p95 ~320ms, cost per 1k tokens about 0.9 vs 2.8 in our estimate, there was some noise in the 4k run (spikes), might be caching behavior
[01:35] Tom Reynolds: a quick note - our dev cluster has slightly different kernel timings so take numbers with a pinch of salt, but the relative diff is clear
[02:05] Aisha Khan: ok that matches what we saw, but we care about hallucination rate too - 13b had a slightly higher FPR on entity extraction tests

[02:30] Sofia Chen: yeah and for the QA tasks we ran, 70b-q4 reduces hallucination on long contexts; the tradeoff is latency/cost. there were occasional tokenization mismatches in the transcript of the test (some names got split)

[03:01] Lena Park: given those tradeoffs our recommendation is pin primary to model-redwood-13b-v2 for low latency routes (search and UX prompts) and configure fallback to 70b-q4 for long-context or high-accuracy routes - that keeps costs down but lets you failover for quality
[03:29] Priya Desai: can you explain how fallback would work in practice? we need deterministic behavior for A/B tests

[03:45] Marco Ruiz: sure - routing policy can be per-route: e.g. production/short-chat -> pinned 13b; production/long-analysis -> pinned 70b-q4. we also support dynamic fallback: on quality regression or if p95 > SLA, system can reroute to a compatible variant. fallback map looks like 13b -> 70b-q4, 13b-quant -> 13b, etc
[04:12] Aisha Khan: is the fallback instant? we're worried about state (kv cache) consistency across model variants

[04:30] Marco Ruiz: good point - fallback does a new request to the fallback model so you lose in-memory KV cache for that session. we do offer prefix/KV cache warming for pinned models, but cross-model cache reuse is limited; that's why we recommend careful canarying
[05:01] Tom Reynolds: we saw in our trial that switching mid-session gave weird continuity issues - names repeated oddly, probably kv mismatch
[05:18] Sofia Chen: yes, we usually recommend session-bound pinning for continuity and only trigger fallback between independent requests or after a soft checkpoint

[05:45] Marco Ruiz: also mentioned quantization caveat - 70b-q4 is quantized which helps cost but sometimes affects rare token distributions, so in legal/regulatory text you might prefer non-quant or additional passing through a reranker
[06:10] Aisha Khan: regulatory content is big for us - we need to ensure we can pin to a non-quant variant if needed and have audit logs
[06:25] Lena Park: yes, audit logs and KMS are supported - sofia will send the security extract after this call, includes SOC2 scope and KMS notes
[06:38] Priya Desai: perfect, we will review that with our compliance team
[07:05] Marco Ruiz: back to performance - we also ran a small continuous-batching config which reduced cost by ~12% for 13b with negligible latency impact; we can enable it for certain routes
[07:30] Tom Reynolds: what's the risk with batching? in bursty traffic it could add latency for first token
[07:42] Marco Ruiz: yes, we can set latency SLO caps and batching windows; default safe config keeps first token at SLA while batching tail requests
[08:10] Aisha Khan: a question on model pinning rollout - can we do a canary with 10% traffic to 70b when we detect quality drop on 13b?

[08:25] Marco Ruiz: absolutely, our rollout supports percentage-based canaries plus metric-based auto-promotion/rollback. the system can configure thresholds on perplexity, regression on your prompt suite, or manual gates
[08:45] Priya Desai: in terms of observability, will we get token-level breakdowns? we want to tie cost to features
[08:52] Lena Park: yes token-level cost and latency per-route is in console, and you can export traces to our tracing hooks; we'll include an example dashboard
[09:10] Tom Reynolds: about rollback, do you have a playbook for sudden perf regression? last time we had to revert containers manually

[09:22] Sofia Chen: we have a standard rollback playbook: 1) shift traffic to fallback model, 2) drain in-flight sessions (optional), 3) run quick bench, 4) if root cause infra, escalate to support; Marco will prep a tailored playbook for your infra
[09:50] Aisha Khan: can we pin versions by digest or by friendly version name? we want deterministic reproducibility for audit
[09:58] Marco Ruiz: you can pin by immutable model digest (recommended) or by version alias; digest is best for audits and rollbacks
[10:12] Lena Park: quick note - we've seen teams pin to a digest for production and keep a version alias for canaries so it's easier to swap during testing
[10:35] Tom Reynolds: on the test infra - i'll run the 4k context throughput test this week, what config should i use?
[10:44] Marco Ruiz: use sequence length 4k, batch sizes increasing from 1 to 8, and enable kv cache, send both 13b and 70b-q4; we'll provide the test script in the repo link
[11:10] Priya Desai: about cost modeling, can you share the spreadsheet with per-route cost and recommendations?
[11:18] Lena Park: yes i'll share a cost/latency sheet, it includes recommended pin map and expected monthly burn for your projected qps
[11:35] Aisha Khan: one small nit - in your earlier sheet the tokenization assumptions were different from ours, names split differently which affected stats
[11:47] Sofia Chen: thanks, we'll align tokenization config and re-run the sample scripts, i'll add notes to the spreadsheet about tokenization settings
[12:10] Tom Reynolds: security question - what about bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and HSM?
[12:20] Sofia Chen: BYOK via KMS supported, HSM integrations on enterprise/private deployments; we'll include the options in the security pack
[12:38] Aisha Khan: good. also we had a question re: data residency - can we force inference in eu-west region?
[12:47] Lena Park: yes regional pinning is supported, you can route EU traffic to eu region endpoints and dedicate capacity if needed (dedicated or private)
[13:05] Priya Desai: timeline check - we want to do a limited canary next week if tests pass, is that realistic?
[13:12] Marco Ruiz: yes if Tom uploads the sysbench logs by Friday we can provision canary and run the rollout Monday, Sofia and i will be on standby
[13:28] Aisha Khan: about fallback continuity again - if we fallback mid-user-journey and lose KV, can we rehydrate from app-side state?
[13:40] Marco Ruiz: apps can send prefix/context manually to rehydrate, it's not automatic across different model families, so engineer-side handling recommended
[14:02] Tom Reynolds: ok we can add rehydration hooks on our side for critical flows

[14:18] Lena Park: quick recap before we wrap - recommended pin: 13b-v2 primary for latency-sensitive routes, fallback to 70b-q4 for accuracy critical; pin by digest in prod; canary plan week of April 5th pending tests; security docs to go out in 48 hours
[14:45] Priya Desai: that sounds good, can you also include a simple decision matrix for which routes get which pin?
[14:53] Marco Ruiz: yes will include a matrix: route type, SLA, pin, fallback, batching suggestion
[15:10] Aisha Khan: also please call out known quantization caveats for regulatory text
[15:20] Sofia Chen: will do, adding a footnote in the pack
[15:35] Lena Park: any final questions?
[15:42] Tom Reynolds: none from infra, i'll run the tests and post logs
[15:50] Priya Desai: none from product, thanks
[16:00] Aisha Khan: thanks all, appreciate it
[16:10] Lena Park: thanks everyone, sending meeting notes and next steps after - bye
[16:20] (call ends)
